title: Simulate round robin with context-switch cost and a multi-level feedback queue
brief: Give every job a turn with a time quantum, then build a scheduler that learns which jobs are interactive by watching how they use the CPU.
hints: Keep a collections.deque of ready jobs. Admit every job with arrival <= clock before you pop, and again after a slice ends but before you push the preempted job back, so arrivals queue ahead of it.
A slice lasts min(quantum, remaining). Charge switch_cost only when the next job differs from the job that just ran and the CPU was not idle in between.

For mlfq, step one tick at a time. Each tick: boost if due, admit arrivals and woken jobs in name order, preempt if a higher queue is non-empty, pick the head of the highest non-empty queue, run one tick, then decide where the job goes.
After the tick, test in this order: finished, then demote if used >= allotment (and the level is not the last), then block for I/O if since_io == io_every, then re-queue if the quantum is used up.
A preempted job goes to the front of its queue, not the back, and gets a fresh quantum when it next runs. Allotment use is kept.
